newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB board adopts plan to issue 766 mln new shares.
newsitem.headline: NCB board adopts plan to issue 766 mln new shares.

text.p: Japan's troubled Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Tuesday that its board formally approved a plan to issue 766.04 million new shares, worth 167 billion yen, in a third-party allotment.
The share issue plan, first unveiled in early April, is designed to increase the bank's capital.
The bank said in a statement that the new shares will be priced at 218 yen each, which it based on NCB's average closing price of 241.60 yen on the Tokyo bourse over the past five sessions.
The payment date is June 30, it said.

The new shares will be allocated to other banks and life and non-life insurance companies, NCB said, adding that those firms had informally agreed to hold the new NCB shares for two years from the issuance.
As for the bank's future plans to raise capital, the bank said it was still considering raising a total of 123.7 billion yen through an issue of preferred stock, which it announced on April 8.
The board's approval of the plan came a day after Nippon Life Insurance Co said that it would accept an NCB request to help the troubled long-term credit bank increase its capital.
Industry sources have said that Nippon Life's decision to buy NCB shares would help convince other financial institutions to accept NCB's plan to boost its capital by 290.7 billion yen.
